title.en: Stanza 2: the sea and the passing of time

hook.en: The same beach, the same waves, decades later. The sea looks almost the same. The girls who paddled in it do not.

objectives.en: Explain the contrast between the sea and the people
Explain the mother's laughter at the snapshot

narration.en: The same beach, the same waves, decades later. The sea looks almost the same. The girls who paddled in it do not.

body.en: In the second stanza the speaker notices that the sea in the picture has changed far less than the girls. The sea seems almost permanent, while human beings grow up, grow old and pass away. The image of the girls' "terribly transient feet" stresses how short a human life is compared with nature.

points.en: The girls: they grow up, age and die
Contrast: permanence of nature vs transience of life

narration.en: In the second stanza the speaker notices that the sea in the picture has changed far less than the girls. The sea seems almost permanent, while human beings grow up, grow old and pass away. The image of the girls' "terribly transient feet" stresses how short a human life is compared with nature.
Let us set the sea against the people in the photograph.

say.en: On one side the sea, on the other the people.
The sea hardly changes; the girls grow old and, in time, die.
The sea lasts; human life is transient, or short-lived.
In the photo the sea washes the feet of the smiling girls.
Years later the sea is the same, but the mother looks back and laughs.

body.en: Some twenty or thirty years later, the mother would look at the snapshot and laugh, pointing out Betty and Dolly and the way the girls had been dressed for the beach. Her laughter is affectionate but tinged with sadness: she is looking back at a childhood she can never return to.

points.en: Twenty or thirty years after the photo
She laughs at the old beach clothes
Nostalgia: fond longing for the past

narration.en: Some twenty or thirty years later, the mother would look at the snapshot and laugh, pointing out Betty and Dolly and the way the girls had been dressed for the beach. Her laughter is affectionate but tinged with sadness: she is looking back at a childhood she can never return to.

problem.en: What does the poet convey through the contrast between the sea and the girls?

steps.en: The sea in the picture has hardly changed over the years.
The girls have grown up and changed; their lives are short.
Nature is lasting; human life is brief.

answer.en: The sea looks almost the same after many years, while the girls have grown old and changed. The contrast shows that nature is lasting, but human life is short and passes quickly.

body.en: Three stanzas, three times. Stanza 1: the Snap (the photograph is taken). Stanza 2: the Smile (the mother laughs at it years later). Stanza 3: the Silence (the mother has died, and the speaker has no words).

points.en: The sea has changed little; the people have changed greatly.
Human life is transient compared with nature.
Years later the mother laughs at the photo, longing for her lost childhood.

homework.en: Write a paragraph on something in your town that has stayed the same while people have changed.
